I recently attended a wedding at Kora Kendar, and while the overall ambience was pleasant, I was disappointed with the lack of proper washroom facilities. Having previously visited for a garba event a few years ago, I expected improvements in this area, but unfortunately, it was still a major inconvenience.

The venue relies on portable restrooms, commonly known as porta-potties, which are known for their discomfort and lack of cleanliness. This arrangement was highly inconvenient, especially during a wedding where guests require comfortable and hygienic washroom facilities. The absence of proper washroom amenities significantly affected the overall experience.

However, it's worth noting that Kora Kendar does excel in terms of ambiance. The atmosphere created for the event was enjoyable, and the management seemed to have put effort into creating a pleasant environment for the guests. The overall decor and arrangements were satisfactory, contributing to the positive aspects of the venue.

Despite the shortcomings in washroom facilities, Kora Kendar may still be a suitable choice for events like garba or weddings, provided that alternative arrangements are made for washroom facilities. It would greatly enhance the overall experience and ensure the comfort of guests.

featured_reviews.name: Aditi Prabhu
featured_reviews.review_text:
Ambiance: Simple, soothing, with both indoor and outdoor sitting. Located at Babhai Naka, Borivali.

Our experience: We went in for dinner on a weekday. The place was largely empty and quiet. Took them 20 mins to take our first order despite having only 4 tables being served including ours.

We ordered the following dishes:
• Bombil Fry: The coating was way too thicker and the bombil hardly present. Could barely taste the bombil.
• Prawn koliwada: Again the coating overpowered the flavor of prawns.
• Bangda Thali and Ravas thali: Both thalis were exactly the same with the same fish curry, a tiny serving of prawn preparation, another tiny serving of matki usal in one thali and another random gravy in the bangda thalis. We weren't asked about our preferences for wada, chapati or bhakri. So one thali came with wadas, the other with chapati and on placing the order the third, we were asked about our preference for chapati or bhakri then informed bhakri is probabaly over. So we okayed chapati but were served wadas.

We also ordered another plate of extra chapati which they didnt have and offered wadas but none reached our table even after 2 reminders.

Finally we finished our meals and then asked for the bill which had the extra cost of wadas which we ordered and never recieved and also for the wada in thali which we weren't informed were charged extra but were given as they didnt have chapatis or bhakris.

They did change the bill on being informed.

We also asked for regular water which we recieved almost at the end of the meal after being reminded for the fifth time.

Service: Slow, and confused even when there were just 2-3 tables with people only.

While we understand it was end if the day and hence the food there was over and also probably that is why there were many errors & delays in service. But the overall experience and food were not upto the mark or hype.

featured_reviews.name: Anagh Pathak
featured_reviews.review_text:
The ISKCON Temple in Juhu, formally known as Sri Sri Radha Rasabihari Temple, is one of Mumbai’s most revered spiritual landmarks. Inaugurated in 1978, the temple was the vision of A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada, who founded the Hare Krishna movement. Built on four acres of land once known as "Hare Krishna Land," the temple stands as a testament to his perseverance. The magnificent structure is crafted from white marble and features a stunning 100-foot dome, making it a "spiritual oasis" that provides a serene contrast to the relentless energy of the surrounding city.

The temple’s architecture is a masterful blend of traditional Indian design and modern functionality. Inside the main hall, visitors are greeted by intricately carved pillars and vibrant murals that depict scenes from the Mahabharata and the life of Lord Krishna. The central altars house the beautifully adorned deities of Sri Sri Radha Rasabihari, Sri Gaura Nitai, and Sri Sita Rama Laxman Hanuman. Throughout the day, the air is filled with the rhythmic chanting of the Maha Mantra and the sound of traditional instruments, creating a meditative atmosphere that draws millions of devotees and tourists each year.

Beyond its religious significance, ISKCON Juhu serves as a comprehensive cultural and educational center. The complex includes the "Heaven on Earth" wing, which features a spacious library of Vedic literature, a guesthouse, and a boutique. A highlight for many is Govinda’s, the in-house restaurant that serves delicious *sattvic* vegetarian cuisine to hundreds of guests daily. Through its various initiatives, including youth programs and Vedic education courses, the temple continues to be a vibrant hub for community service and spiritual growth, remaining a cornerstone of Mumbai's cultural fabric.

I’ve been meaning to go to this place for a long time since I heard so much about it…but yesterday finally got the chance - and must say it was quite an amazing experience with friends. We sat at the garden area open air and it was beautiful - though the day had been oppressively hot, the evening was pretty chill and with the big fans doing their bit - we felt right at home. I mean, if you live in hot muggy Mumbai, what’s a little sweaty shirt sticking to your back while you have an evening full of fun with friends.

Okay, now for the food. Must say that since the new caterers took over the management a while back - the menu is pretty exhaustive with Indian and Chinese dishes on the menu. In non veg starters I highly recommend the prawns tempura as also the bhuna tandoori murgh. It’s delectable. Also the basil chilli chicken was a discovery.For the main course we ordered Chinese veg fried rice with chilli chicken and I quite liked the authentic Chinese taste (it is not Indianised Chinese fare).

For dessert we had the caramel pudding and mango and malai kulfi. All superb.

The pricing is the main attraction as I guess everything is subsidised because it is an army club. Really worth it as we each ended up paying rs.1000/-₹ per head for food and drink and that was so awesome.

So why the 4 stars ⭐️ you might ask? Well, the service at the tables leaves a bit to be desired. If you are in the AC section, you have to come all the way out to the bar for your drinks as they don’t serve alcohol on the table. And the dips and chutneys are nothing to write home about. Also, the dress code (for men formal tucked in shirts, leather shoes no sneakers) is a bit of a tedium. Also, you need an officer friend to sign you in and you can’t just walk in there. So, in a nutshell a great outdoor place with a bit of old world charm - and easy on the pocket. Go for it…

featured_reviews.name: Priyanka
featured_reviews.review_text:
### **Review for Prithvi Café**
Prithvi Café is legendary for its vibe and history, but if I’m being honest, the food felt a bit overhyped. It’s a great spot to hang out, but the flavors were a hit-or-miss for me :(

So, I was leaving for out of India but just wanted to explore this cafe before leaving as I will be missing Indian food a little!
But, I kind of got disappointed with the food. To be honest the dishes I had at airport were better🥲

**The Food Breakdown:**
🌟 Egg Kheema: Just okay. It didn't quite live up to the expectations I had based on the reviews.
🌟 Butter Chicken Thali: This was a letdown. The gravy was **way too sweet**—even for Butter Chicken. It lacked that savory, spicy balance you'd expect.
🌟 Mixed Veg Paratha: One of the better items we ordered. Solid, filling, and tasted fresh.
🌟 Burger (Must Try!): The highlight of the meal. The bun isn't made of maida (refined flour), which gave it a great texture. Definitely worth a try if you want something "healthier" but tasty.
Chocolate Croissant: A decent sweet finish, but nothing groundbreaking.

**Drinks:**
We tried the Blueberry Soda and Masala Soda. Both were refreshing and served as good palate cleansers for the meal.

Go for the atmosphere and the non-maida burgers, but maybe skip the North Indian mains if you aren't a fan of sweet gravies. It's a nice place to chill, just don't expect a culinary masterpiece across the whole menu.

Juhu Prices That Won’t Hurt Your Pocket

Recently visited Prithvi Cafe, tucked inside the iconic Prithvi Theatre complex, and the vibe is just as charming as everyone says. There’s also a small bookstore inside, which adds to the overall artsy, cozy feel of the place.

Coming to the waiting system

Now the food

Paneer cheese stuffed kulcha with chole, with chaas and mango lassi – too delicious!  ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

featured_reviews.name: The explorer
featured_reviews.review_text: Inspite of visiting a couple of times before, we've never shot pictures to upload in the review as this was a busy place that involved queue system to be seated. Our last visit was on a weekday afternoon and hence we got a table without a wait time. The seating is outdoor and the menu is pocket friendly and extensive. Most of their kitchen seems outdoor and causes fumes,sizzles and fragrances of multiple dishes being cooked. The dining is moderately under dhaded trees and thoroughly placed table fans. The menu and ordering are online while the bill can be paid once your are  about to leave. Service staff are busy but give you attention when needed. Our asked for extra plate/spoon have immediately been fulfilled. The orders once placed have also arrived quick to the table. We've been ordering from this place for years and hence have reordered most of our favorites to enjoy them fresh which include their paratha with dal makhani, red velvet brownie and cookies. Their sulemani chai and masala soda were well made too. No excessive sugars in the beverages that we ordered. Overall it was a nostalgic place for us and being able to dine without a wait time is a plus.

featured_reviews.name: Shruti Goyal
featured_reviews.review_text: The food was top-notch, especially the hummus absolutely delicious! However, the waiting time for a table was too long due to the excessive crowd. Most of the time, I ended up leaving without eating, and on several occasions, I walked out rather than wait. I usually prefer to get food from somewhere else instead of waiting that long. Overall, great food, but service speed and crowd management need. improvement.

featured_reviews.name: Mayur Aundhakar
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited **Prithvi Café** and had a really good experience overall. The café has a beautiful, lively ambience with a chilled, artsy vibe — perfect for casual meetups or relaxed meals.

I tried quite a few dishes here:
🍽️ **Amritsari Paratha** – Nicely stuffed, flavorful, and served hot with curd and chutney. The taste was authentic and had a pleasant spicy punch without being overpowering.
🍝 **White Pasta** – Creamy, rich, and perfectly cooked. The sauce was smooth and mildly cheesy, though it could use a little more spice for those who like stronger flavors.
☕ **Hot Coffee & Filter Coffee Ice-Cream** – Both were excellent. The hot coffee was strong and aromatic, while the filter coffee ice-cream was a unique treat — a perfect balance of bitterness and sweetness.
🥭 **Mango Lassi** – Thick, fresh, and refreshing, with a real mango flavor. It paired well with the paratha and gave a nice desi touch to the meal.
🌯 **Chicken Roll** – Juicy, well-marinated, and wrapped in soft bread. Nicely spiced and filling; non-veg lovers will definitely enjoy this.

The **service** was polite and quick despite the crowd. **Pricing** is slightly on the higher side, but the taste and ambience justify it. The **outdoor seating** under trees gives a cozy, café-theatre vibe that’s hard to find elsewhere in Mumbai.

✅ **Overall:** Quite good experience — tasty food, soothing coffee, and vibrant atmosphere. A must-visit if you’re near Juhu, especially for coffee lovers and café enthusiasts

featured_reviews.name: Bazooka
featured_reviews.review_text: MIG Building in Tilak Nagar is part of an older residential setup, but it still works well as a practical place to live. The building is around 12 floors high and has a good functional elevator, which makes daily movement much easier, especially in a taller residential block. One thing that stands out positively is that two apartments on the 8th floor have been kept open for fire evacuation use, which is actually a reassuring safety feature and not something you see often in older buildings. The overall vibe is simple and residential rather than modern or premium, but it has a solid community feel. A big plus is the open view from higher floor (with a sunset and sunrise view) especially overlooking the station side and surrounding area…which makes the place feel less cramped than many typical city apartments . The location is also very convenient, with easy access to Tilak Nagar station(just 3 mins away), roads, markets, and daily essentials nearby. Since it’s an older building, some parts may feel a bit dated compared to newer societies, overall it’s a reliable and functional residential option with good connectivity and a few thoughtful practical features that make everyday living decent.
